Note: this is the first draft in the corpus with category std and submissiontype IETF; the others are exp and independent. That fits a document that updates RFC 8620 and RFC 9425.

Open before posting: the email address of Mark's datatracker login (the API 'user' field). It may not be mark@reviewcommit.com. Ask.

Procedure (datatracker submission API, per https://datatracker.ietf.org/api/submission, checked 2026-11-15; no API key, XML-only uploads, multipart/form-data so use curl, not wget):

1. Build and check, from /data/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec (S = session scratchpad):
     kramdown-rfc draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00.md > $S/draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00.xml
     xml2rfc --text $S/draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00.xml -o $S/draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00.txt   # expect no warnings
     /data/ietf-tools/node/bin/idnits $S/draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00.txt
   Fix every idnits error and any warning that isn't a known false positive; commit and push the fix first, so the posted -00 matches the repo.

2. Submit (after go-ahead):
     curl -s -F "user=<datatracker login>" -F "xml=@$S/draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00.xml" https://datatracker.ietf.org/api/submission
   Success: JSON {id, name, rev, status_url}. Failure: {"error": "..."}. If the error says submissions are closed, the post-meeting-cutoff window has not reopened yet; stop and tell Mark.

     curl -s https://datatracker.ietf.org/api/submission/<id>/status

5. Verify https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-atwood-jmap-updates/ resolves and shows -00. Update 0577 if the URL differs. Then close this bead, which unblocks 0577.
"}
